title: Thirtieth Post-Cabinet Press Briefing 2026
primaryAgendaItem: 2026/27 drought resilience plan; Harare vending formalisation; health sector update; climate and international cooperation
summary: Cabinet approved the 2026/27 Summer Plan incorporating a six-pillar drought plan, measures to address informal vending in Harare, the July 2026 health-sector update, the Chartered Secretaries (Private) Amendment Bill, and a Zimbabwe-Sweden environment and climate cooperation MoU. Cabinet also received reports on solar cooperation, Zimbabwe-China economic and technical cooperation, the Non-Aligned Movement commemoration and Zimbabwe's participation at the 76th WHO Regional Committee for Africa.

highlights.detail: Cabinet approved six resilience pillars: enhanced Strategic Grain Reserve; accelerated climate-smart production; integrated financing; livestock drought mitigation; enhanced imports; and coordination, early-warning systems and capacity-building.

National cereal production for 2026/27 is expected at 1.6 million metric tonnes, with a Strategic Grain Reserve target of 600,000 metric tonnes and an expected cereal deficit of 266,881 to 541,881 metric tonnes.
The private sector will be allowed to import to meet commercial needs for both food and feed, while household basic-food import provisions will continue and are to be reviewed upwards.
Cabinet approved measures based on Legislate, Provide, Formalise and Enforce, including servicing 100 vending sites, a new satellite market and a 60-day one-stop formalisation drive.

Cabinet noted outcomes of the Eighth International Solar Alliance Regional Committee for Africa, including STAR-C at Chinhoyi University of Technology, the Solar Universal Gender Assessment Tool, the Zimbabwe-ISA Country Partnership Framework and the Solar Agriculture for She pact.

Cabinet approved the July 2026 Health Sector Update, noting implementation of the National Health Strategy 2026-2030, health financing and workforce measures, medicines availability, immunisation, maternal health, cervical cancer services, epidemic preparedness and cholera response.
Cabinet approved the Chartered Secretaries (Private) Amendment Bill, 2026 to modernise the institute and broaden governance, accountancy, auditing and related professional education and regulation.

Cabinet approved an MoU on environment, climate and sustainable natural-resource use, covering capacity-building, pollution reduction, carbon trading, climate mitigation and enhanced weather and climate early-warning services.

Cabinet noted the 11th JETC session, including trade and investment cooperation, China's Unified Quarantine Announcements for selected products, value addition, e-commerce, digital trade, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
Cabinet approved Zimbabwe's report from RC76. Six SADC Member States agreed to establish a technical committee to explore a Regional Medicines and Health Commodities Pooled Procurement Initiative.

sourceNote: Structured from the published 30th Post-Cabinet media briefing presented in Harare on 16 September 2026 and published by The Herald on 17 September 2026.
